notes: Both PEPlife2 values verified exactly against Table 1: tau1/2 alpha 15.7 ± 0.8 h and tau1/2 beta 15.9 ± 0.9 h. The two phases are within 0.2 h of each other, so these are effectively one number reported twice rather than two separable phases, and counting both double-weights this single N = 5 experiment. The body itself quotes only the beta value. REPRESENTATION MISMATCH: PEPlife2's sequence is the bare 28-residue thymosin alpha 1 peptide, but the dosed agent is Tα1 fused to a 600-RESIDUE PAS polypeptide - the paper's whole point, 'fusion with a 600-residue polypeptide comprising the small natural L-amino acids Pro, Ala, and Ser', biophysically mimicking PEG. The stored sequence is therefore about 5% of the molecule by length, while the label is entirely a product of the missing 95%. For reference the body gives the native peptide's published rat half-life as 1.9 h. Note also tmax is 22.7 h, longer than the half-life itself, so this subcutaneous profile is absorption-rate-limited (flip-flop) and the terminal value reflects depot release rather than clearance.
